root_cause.text: The arm64 BPF JIT allocated the JIT image with only 4-byte alignment, so build_plt() could place struct bpf_plt's u64 target field at a misaligned address, breaking the required 8-byte alignment for atomic concurrent access in bpf_arch_text_poke().
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes bpf_jit_binary_pack_alloc() alignment from sizeof(u32) to sizeof(u64), and the CVE/commit explicitly states that with 4-byte-aligned JIT buffers the padding logic in build_plt() “fails to ensure that target lands on an 8-byte boundary,” causing misaligned u64 access and possible torn reads while WRITE_ONCE() updates target concurrently with JIT code executing ldr.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix JIT binary pack allocation to use 64-bit sizing/alignment instead of 32-bit when allocating the BPF JIT image.
intent_record.what: The call to bpf_jit_binary_pack_alloc() was changed to pass sizeof(u64) instead of sizeof(u32) as its size/alignment-related argument during JIT image allocation.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes the allocated JIT binary pack use 64-bit sizing/alignment rather than 32-bit, which prevents the generated image/header layout from being based on an undersized width and avoids incorrect placement or alignment on 64-bit expectations.

grouping_result.intent: Fix JIT binary pack allocation to use 64-bit sizing/alignment instead of 32-bit when allocating the BPF JIT image.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by correcting the BPF JIT image allocation sizing/alignment from 32-bit/4-byte to 64-bit/8-byte, preventing misalignment of the struct bpf_plt u64 target field used by build_plt() and bpf_arch_text_poke().

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
bpf, arm64: use bpf_prog_pack for memory management

Use bpf_jit_binary_pack_alloc for memory management of JIT binaries
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 1dad391daef129e01e28206b8d586608ff026548
Author: Puranjay Mohan <puranjay@kernel.org>
Date:   Wed Feb 28 14:18:24 2024 +0000

    bpf, arm64: use bpf_prog_pack for memory management
    
    Use bpf_jit_binary_pack_alloc for memory management of JIT binaries in
    ARM64 BPF JIT. The bpf_jit_binary_pack_alloc creates a pair of RW and RX
    buffers. The JIT writes the program into the RW buffer. When the JIT is
    done, the program is copied to the final RX buffer
    with bpf_jit_binary
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the JIT image allocation logic in `bpf_int_jit_compile()`, which is the relevant place for the alignment bug. The root cause is that the arm64 BPF JIT allocated the image with only 4-byte alignment, allowing the PLT target `u64` to become misaligned. In this commit, allocation is still done with `bpf_jit_binary_pack_alloc(image_size, &ro_image_ptr, sizeof(u32), &header, &image_ptr, jit_fill_hole);` where the alignment argument is explicitly `sizeof(u32)`. That is only 4 bytes. The code also computes `extable_offset = round_up(prog_size + PLT_TARGET_SIZE, extable_align);` and the comment says `/* also allocate space for plt target */`, confirming the same image contains the PLT target area. Since the allocation alignment remains 4 bytes, the base of the JIT image may be only 4-byte aligned, so a `u64` PLT target inside that image can still land at a non-8-byte-aligned address. Nothing in this function changes the allocation alignment to 8 bytes or otherwise guarantees 8-byte alignment for the PLT target. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present (`has_bug=true`) and the fix is not yet present (`is_fixed=false`).

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:

The JIT compiler emits A64 instructions. It supports eBPF only.
Legacy BPF is supported thanks
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit e54bcde3d69d40023ae77727213d14f920eb264a
Author: Zi Shen Lim <zlim.lnx@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Aug 26 21:15:30 2014 -0700

    arm64: eBPF JIT compiler
    
    The JIT compiler emits A64 instructions. It supports eBPF only.
    Legacy BPF is supported thanks to conversion by BPF core.
    
    JIT is enabled in the same way as for other architectures:
    
            echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/core/bpf_jit_enable
    
    Or for additional compiler output:
    
            echo 2 > /proc/sys
bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant allocation logic is shown directly in `bpf_int_jit_compile()`, so the snippet is sufficient. The vulnerable construct is present at `ctx.image = module_alloc(image_size);`. The root cause says the arm64 BPF JIT allocated the JIT image with only 4-byte alignment, which could later misalign a `struct bpf_plt` `u64 target` field. This initial implementation simply uses `image_size = sizeof(u32) * ctx.idx;` and then `module_alloc(image_size);`, with no extra alignment or padding to guarantee 8-byte alignment for later data structures embedded in the JIT image. There is also no logic anywhere in this function to round the allocation size/alignment up to 8 bytes or otherwise ensure `struct bpf_plt` placement is 8-byte aligned. Therefore the vulnerable allocation pattern is present, and the fix is not present.
